title: The Cold Border
premise: Ivo Okafor, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent a decade erasing herself so thoroughly that even her own file reads like fiction. When Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight, she realizes the plane's lone passenger, a defector named Sable, is a lure designed to flush out people like her: people the Group has decided never existed. Extracting Sable across three frozen borders, Ivo discovers the defector carries proof of Ivo's erased identity, and that her handler—the closest thing she has to family—is the one who sold her. In the end, Ivo chooses to stop disappearing: she burns her old self deliberately, gives Sable the evidence, and walks into a new life built not on invisibility but on the fragile found family of the people who chose her.
about_author: Oscar Nystrom is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent years working contracts near border zones and never quite says which ones. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be unmemorable.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine night in Riga: Ivo cleans up a diplomat's indiscretion, checks her go-bag, and trades dry banter with her handler, Marek, who teases her about having no past. Establishes her competence, her loneliness, and the Group's rules. Emotional beat: the comfort of a life built on routine and erasure.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A passenger jet lands with its records scrubbed—no manifest, no flight plan, no trace it ever flew. Ivo is ordered to retrieve the sole unlisted passenger, a defector codenamed Sable, before rival services do. She realizes the erasure technology is the Group's own. Emotional beat: the first crack of unease—the tools of her invisibility turned against someone else.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In a safehouse outside Vilnius, Ivo meets Sable—a sharp, terrified analyst who claims she was never on any plane; she woke up in one. She carries a drive she won't open, saying only that it contains names the Group deleted. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people trained not to trust.

chapters.title: Three Borders by Dawn
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A brutal overland extraction as a hostile service closes in, forcing Ivo to improvise through checkpoints and a frozen rail yard. Sable proves unexpectedly resourceful, saving Ivo's cover at a border crossing. Emotional beat: the first flicker of partnership—found family beginning to form under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Drive Says
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hiding in a disused lighthouse, Sable finally opens the drive: personnel files of operatives erased by the Group—including one for a girl named Ivo Okafor, listed as terminated twelve years ago. Sable realizes Ivo doesn't know what she is. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness—knowing a truth that will break someone you're starting to care about.

chapters.title: The Handler's Hand
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A dead-drop goes wrong; the ambush uses protocols only Marek knows. Confronting him by phone, Ivo hears him confess, almost gently, that she was always the mission—the defector is bait to confirm the erased can be found. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only family she had, and the vertigo of a self that was never hers.

chapters.title: Terminated, Twelve Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ivo and Sable's alternating POV. Ivo reads her own file: recruited as a teenager, wiped, rebuilt. She spirals—every memory now suspect—while Sable grounds her: the file proves what was done to her, not who she is. Emotional beat: the identity crisis at its darkest, and the choice to keep going anyway.

chapters.title: The Meridian Trap
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo turns the bait around: she feeds the Group false coordinates, luring Marek's kill team into the open at a Baltic port. The plan works too well—the trap catches Sable instead. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into resolve; the price of survival becomes someone else's life.

chapters.title: Cold Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax. On the frozen harbor, Ivo trades herself for Sable, then turns Marek's own erasure protocol against the Group, broadcasting the deleted files to every embassy that doesn't exist. She fights Marek on the ice; he falls through, and she—unlike the Group—tries to save him. Emotional beat: Ivo refuses to become what they made her.

chapters.title: A Name She Chooses
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Weeks later: the Group is gutted, its secrets public. Ivo, legally nonexistent, sits with Sable and the two surviving erased operatives at a kitchen table in a country no one would look for her in. She unpacks the go-bag for the first time in a decade. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—identity not recovered but chosen, family not found but kept.
